subject: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing — Finova follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Finova — post-demo: performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Hi John / Priya,

Great to speak with you this morning — thanks for walking through the Finova use case and latency expectations. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of requirements we captured on the call:
- Latency: target p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 200ms for non-streamed responses (for typical 256-token responses).
- Streaming: partial/first-byte latency for streaming must be <= 120ms for interactive flows.
- Throughput: expected baseline ~350 QPS across the account, peak bursts to ~1,200 QPS.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency target 250 concurrent streams; want headroom for 400 during peak events.
- Daily tokens: ~1.2M tokens/day (estimate from your product team).
- Multi-region routing: primary routing split US (primary), EU (for EU customers with data residency), APAC as warm-fallback.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU zones (storage, logs, and KV caches).

Ask / next steps
1) We can run a 2-week PoC focusing on: (a) latency p95 validation (non-stream and streaming), (b) concurrency soak to your peak, (c) multi-region routing verification with EU-only residency.
2) Please confirm whether the 200ms p95 is measured as: end-to-end server-side processing (Redwood only), or includes network RTT to your clients; we assume server-side processing for SLO definition.
3) Agree on PoC week — we propose Apr 19-30 window.

I've attached a draft SLO calculation workbook and a mutual action plan that maps responsibilities and milestones. Aditya and Dev are cc'd to scope the benchmark.

Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: redwood-slo-calculation.xlsx (xlsx), mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)

From: John Lee <john.lee@finova.com>

Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@finova.com>
Date: 2026-04-05T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova — post-demo: performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications before we lock in PoC dates: 

1) For streaming: when you say "first-byte <= 120ms" is that first-byte at the Redwood edge (server-side) or does it include any client networking? We need to be able to commit to an SLA that our UX team measures from browser-to-first-byte.
2) On the data residency point: our legal team requires that EU customer payloads (including any transient KV cache data) stay in EU. Does Redwood support per-tenant regional KV caches and block cross-region replication for those tenants?
3) For throughput: the 1.2M tokens/day is a ballpark; during quarter-end in Nov we could see a 3x spike. Can the PoC include a stress test to 3.6M tokens/day equivalent and report cost/throughput numbers?

If you can confirm the above, we'll confirm attendees (infra + security) and get back on PoC scheduling.

— John
Senior Engineering Manager, Finova
john.lee@finova.com

Subject: Re: Finova — post-demo: performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

John — great questions, answers below (frankly we should have clarified on the call). Short answers first, details after: 

- Streaming first-byte p95: measured server-side (Redwood edge/ingest) for the PoC/SLO. For an end-to-end UX SLA you should add client-network RTT; we'll provide guidance on a reference client-side measurement.
- Per-tenant KV caches & residency: yes — Redwood supports per-tenant, per-region KV caches and you can opt-out of cross-region replication for EU tenants. Audit logs and stored artifacts for EU tenants remain in EU.
- Stress test: we can include a stress run that scales up to 3.6M tokens/day equivalent; we'll run an autoscaling profile and provide cost/throughput metrics and a summary report.

Detailed notes / technical approach:
1) SLO definitions
   - Non-streamed generation: server-side p95 measured from request accept by Redwood control plane to final token emitted by model runtime. Target: <=200ms.
   - Streaming: first-byte (first token) measured server-side from request accept to first token. Target: <=120ms.
   - Concurrency: we will validate sustained 250 concurrent streams with a 400-stream spike window (5 minutes).
2) Regional routing & residency
   - Routing policy: requests from EU users will be routed to EU-only endpoints (model runtime + storage). US requests route to US endpoints. APAC will be configured as a warm fallback region; we will not replicate EU tenant data to APAC.
   - Caching: KV caches are configurable per-tenant; for EU tenants we'll disable cross-region replication. Ephemeral caches used for prefix/KV acceleration are stored in-region.
3) PoC scope & artifacts
   - Deliverables: SLO validation report, throughput/cost summary, configuration playbook (routing + cache settings), and signed mutual action plan.
   - Attachments: redwood-slo-calculation.xlsx (SLO math + sample load profile), mutual-action-plan.docx (milestones & responsibilities).

Can you confirm: infra + security will join the PoC kickoff (30–45 min) and point us to a contact who can create test accounts and allowbench traffic egress to the Redwood PoC endpoints? Once you confirm I'll lock Apr 20 (Tuesday) 9:30am PT as the kickoff unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa / John — quick technical notes from runtime/bench team: 

Planned PoC test plan (high level):
- Kickoff: 30–45m with Finova infra + security to provision test tenants and confirm endpoints.
- Latency tests: 10k synthetic requests at each payload size (64/256/512 tokens) against US/EU endpoints; measure p50/p95/p99 for non-stream and first-byte for stream.
- Concurrency soak: 6-hour run at 250 sustained concurrent streams with 5-minute 400-stream spike window.
- Stress throughput: simulated burst to 3.6M tokens/day with autoscaler enabled; collect cost metrics.

Technical notes:
- We'll provide an open-source harness (link below) you can run from your network to simulate realistic client RTT. For PoC SLOs we're measuring server-side; we'll also provide a reference script to measure browser-to-first-byte.
- KV cache: will be configured per-tenant and pinned to region; no cross-region replication for EU tenants during PoC.
- Logs/audit: we'll provide a stripped subset of audit logs for security review; full logs remain behind customer-managed KMS.

Proposed kickoff: Apr 20, 09:30 PT. If that works I'll send an invite and a shared Drive folder with the harness and runbook.

Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
